A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and proposed evaluation adjustment. Their main text, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, fine-tuning interventions, regression analyses, and emergence experiments, with additional results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds learning-rate sensitivity, alternative temporal cutoffs, and instruction/chat-model evaluations.

M1.justification: The proposed adjustment remains full-parameter fine-tuning on the same sufficient task-relevant data before evaluation. The main datasets and three-epoch procedure are retained. Changes to the controlled validation experiment and hyperparameter sensitivity tests concern evaluation rather than a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MMLU, GSM8K, ARC, HellaSwag, MMLU Pro, GPQA, BBH, MuSR, and MATH Level 5, using the same task-relevant fine-tuning datasets. The Leaderboard v2 experiments already appear in v1 Appendix C. Added instruction/chat models are evaluated on existing tasks; no instruction-following benchmark is added.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison set expands from 53 to 56 base models, adding Qwen2-0.5B, Qwen2-1.5B, and Qwen2-7B. Appendix F additionally reports comparisons involving 36 instruction/chat models, including Vicuna, Llama 2 Chat, and Qwen1.5 Chat variants. These additions substantially broaden the models compared before and after adjustment.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 changes its reported design from randomly partitioning older models into treatment/control groups to comparing original models with fine-tuned copies, restricting treatment to models with at least 7×10^21 pretraining FLOPs. New protocols include a five-value learning-rate sweep and September 2023/January 2024 cutoffs. The final displayed GSM8K emergence checkpoint also changes from 1.6 million to 320,000 training examples.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.3 tests whether hyperparameter selection favors older models, while Appendix C.1 tests sensitivity to the temporal cutoff. Conversely, v1 Appendix B.3 and Figure 13, which directly examine late-training saturation, are removed. The existing language-based split and model-discrimination analyses are retained under new appendix numbering.

E5.justification: Both versions report regression standard errors and mark statistical significance at p<0.05. The causal tables retain the same uncertainty reporting, and new experiments use existing conventions. No new repeated-run counts, seed disclosures, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: With the expanded model cohort, Figure 1's unadjusted MMLU/GSM8K recency gaps change from 0.068/0.168 to 0.073/0.191. Figure 3 reports different estimates under its revised control design. New Figure 19 reports instruction/chat gaps of 0.063/0.154 unadjusted and -0.001/0.027 adjusted. Robustness results are added and saturation results removed; these are not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6), the causal graph, piecewise log-linear specification, and direct/mediated-effect derivations are retained. The hard-intervention interpretation still requires saturation. Its empirical justification changes, but the formal assumption and mathematical analysis do not.

C1.justification: The central claims about confounded model comparisons, fine-tuning adjustment, and emergence remain. Section 7 modestly narrows the emergence conclusion: v1 says adjustment removes unpredictability and discontinuity, whereas v2 says it greatly reduces unpredictability and makes capabilities predictable at smaller scales.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 newly emphasizes that base-model performance may not predict performance after adaptation. Appendix F explains instruction/chat trends through benchmark-containing instruction data and a shift from preference-oriented to benchmark-oriented post-training. Appendix B now supports saturation indirectly through performance equalization after removing the dedicated saturation analysis.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents few-shot counts and clarifies that MMLU's auxiliary training data come from other benchmarks rather than an IID MMLU split. It adds model repositories, base-model mappings, and learning-rate sweep details, and revises metadata such as Gemma-2B's pretraining tokens from 2T to 3T. The main optimizer, hardware, and code-access disclosures remain.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds an adaptation-before-evaluation subsection connecting the proposal to prior arguments for controlling adaptation resources. It expands the distinction from data contamination and acknowledges closely related emergence findings by Snell et al. and evaluation recommendations by Gu et al. These additions substantially develop the methodological positioning beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution summary, experimental explanations, and discussion undergo broad paragraph-level rewriting. Robustness material is reorganized from Appendix B into a dedicated Appendix C, and the later appendices receive a revised organization. The main seven-section outline remains, but exposition and appendix navigation change substantially.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redesigned from six panels to four. The original emergence Figures 8–9 are regrouped by benchmark into v2 Figures 8 and 18, moving GSM8K to the appendix. New sensitivity, cutoff, and instruction/chat figures and a model table are added; the saturation figure is removed. Several retained figures also receive axis-label and layout refinements.

improvement.justification: The learning-rate and temporal-cutoff checks address concrete alternative explanations, while instruction/chat evaluations strengthen applicability beyond base models. Clearer data descriptions and prior-work positioning also help. However, removing v1 Appendix B.3's direct saturation evidence leaves the causal intervention assumption less directly supported. The added validation provides a net improvement, tempered by that loss.
